podcasts.title: Scott Kupor on Building a16z and Rebuilding the Federal Workforce
podcasts.summary: Scott Kupor helped build a16z from three people into a firm with hundreds of employees. Now, as Director of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management, he’s applying some of the same lessons about talent, incentives, and organizational design to a workforce of roughly two million federal employees. Scott joins Founders host David Senra to tell the story of a16z’s earliest days, from joining Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz during the 2008 financial crisis to borrowing Michael Ovitz’s CAA model to build a venture firm around specialized networks and services for founders. He explains why a16z chose to market itself when venture firms traditionally didn’t, how early wins like Skype accelerated the firm’s growth, and why it eventually reorganized around specialized investing teams. Then they turn to Scott’s move into government. He lays out his effort to build a more merit-based federal workforce, attract younger technical talent, and create what he calls “permissioned risk” so government employees can actually try new things. That includes everything from changing how performance and promotions work to replacing a retirement process that still relied on hundreds of millions of pieces of paper stored in an underground Pennsylvania mine. podcasts.title: The Health Interventions Actually Worth Your Time | Justin Mares
podcasts.summary: Health advice has become an endless stream of supplements, diets, wearables, and biohacks. Which interventions are actually worth your time? Truemed CEO Justin Mares argues that most people should ignore the extremes and focus on a few fundamentals: better food, movement, sleep, and reducing harmful exposures. Justin joins a16z General Partner Daisy Wolf to walk through his own approach to health, from what he eats and how he exercises to supplements, blood tests, sauna, sleep, and the changes he’s made to his home. They also discuss the larger problem behind Truemed: while chronic disease drives the vast majority of U.S. healthcare spending, relatively little goes toward prevention. Justin explains how Truemed is trying to change that by making it easier for eligible consumers to use tax-free HSA and FSA dollars on qualified lifestyle interventions. podcasts.title: Many of the most popular AI benchmarks are badly made. The flaws are easy to build in and hard to ca
podcasts.summary: Many of the most popular AI benchmarks are badly made. The flaws are easy to build in and hard to catch. “A lot of the really popular benchmarks out there are kind of trash. This is largely because they’re made by people who don’t have expertise in making evals or environments or training data in general.” “It’s very easy to make a task that seems good on a surface level, but it’s actually unfair in some way, such that it’s a poor test of model capabilities.” “A lot of people make their tasks harder by making them unfair rather than actually making the task difficult.” “It’s very hard to figure this out unless you run ten rollouts, look at the transcripts, see why the model failed, and determine manually: was this actually a legitimate failure?” Watch the Full Podcast on YouTube.

podcasts.title: Tokenization, Agentic Trading, Harmonic: Robinhood's Mission to Expand Ownership with CEO Vlad Tenev
podcasts.summary: What does it mean to build wealth as an individual investor in today’s society, especially as gains continue to get concentrated into smaller groups of VCs or institutional investors? Robinhood’s CEO and co-founder Vlad Tenev has a vision that can be summed up in one word: Ownership. In this episode, Sarah Guo chats with Vlad to get a closer look at how Robinhood has evolved from a simple app to buy stocks at zero commission into a global conglomerate that allows customers to own across a wide variety of surfaces and asset classes. Vlad explains how Robinhood is helping users extend ownership amidst the current economy and ongoing AI revolution through Trump accounts, tokenization of privates, and newer product offerings like Robinhood Chain, Agentic Trading, and Agentic Credit Card. He also talks about how his new mathematical superintelligence startup, Harmonic, is revolutionizing the field and how he hopes it will decentralize new discoveries and inventions. Vlad and Sarah also discuss how prediction markets could tie into the ownership conversation, whether financial infrastructure can be optimized to enable even higher volumes of high-frequency trading, and his advice for maintaining a level head when facing the vagaries of a changing financial market. podcasts.title: Opportunistic Real Estate and Hard Asset Credit at Mavik – Vik Uppal (EP.525)
podcasts.summary: Vik Uppal is the Founder and CIO of Mavik Capital Management, a $2 billion flexible special situations investment firm grounded in commercial real estate and hard assets that operates through a credit lens. Vik began developing properties as a teenager and after a difficult experience during the financial crisis, moved to New York to begin a career as a professional investor. Our conversation covers Vik's path from developer to distressed investor and the principles he built Mavik around: stable capital, alignment, flexibility, and finding opportunities where capital is scarce. We discuss filtering a wide funnel for ideas, creating downside protection, identifying opportunities in commercial real estate, avoiding the AI infrastructure boom, and growing an investment business without losing its edge.
